messages:
dmitri: Heads up — saw a 8-node TP job intermittently hang on step 42 during model warmup. No CUDA OOMs, but wallclock stalls for ~60s then NCCL timeout.
ben: Can you paste the runtime logs around the hang? any kernel_selector messages or fallback paths?
dmitri: Pasting the relevant slices. look for 'chosen' vs 'fallback' lines and the all-reduce wait:

```
[2026-02-28T14:12:32Z] kernel_selector: chosen kernel=model_gemm_qint8_fast (quantized path)
[2026-02-28T14:12:32Z] kvcache: shard=3 size=1.2GB cap=1.3GB
[2026-02-28T14:12:33Z] kernel_selector: fallback to model_gemm_fp16_soft due to mem_pressure
[2026-02-28T14:13:34Z] nccl: Allreduce timeout on comm 0x7fb... waiting ranks [2,5]
[2026-02-28T14:13:34Z] runtime: detected rank desync, entering slow-path
```

(repro command): ./run_tp_job --nodes 8 --tp 4 --batch 1 --seed 42 --trace-level perf

carmen: Hmm kv-cache near cap when fallback happens — memory churn could change buffer alignment and cause the quantized kernel not to be picked. we've seen alignment-related colective issues before when using int8 kernels.

alice: Do we have kernel selector knobs? maybe force the optimized kernel to see if it reproduces without fallback.

ben: There is an env var: REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer_fast_qint8 which forces selection. Also try REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=1 to remove batching heuristics.

dmitri: Ran with REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=prefer_fast_qint8 and REDWOOD_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=1. Improved — hang rate dropped from ~30% to ~10% but still repro occasionally. Logs now show fast_qint8 chosen most of the time, but occasionally the code paths show 'kv_shard_rebalance' right before the allreduce.

elaine: Could be a race between KV shard eviction and the collective starting — if a shard callback runs on the same stream and blocks kernel launch, NCCL can time out. Do we have a trace that shows stream IDs/timings? try --collectives-trace and --stream-trace.

ci-bot: Perf trace uploaded: link: https://ci.internal/reports/2098765432/trace.json

dmitri: Uploaded a trimmed flame snippet (attached). Observations: compute kernels on stream 2, then kv-evict callback on stream 0 invoked by background GC, then allreduce on stream 2 stalls waiting for something on stream 0 (no explicit sync) — suspected cross-stream resource dependency.

ben: That matches a known bug where cudaEventSynchronize was missing before launching NCCL from a different stream after an async memfree. Quick test: add an explicit cudaStreamWaitEvent before the allreduce for the GC completion and rerun.

alice: If that fixes it, we should add a conservative barrier in the runtime around kv cache evicts that race with collectives. But we need a narrow fix — maybe only when kernel==qint8 and kvcache load > 0.8.

carmen: Also check alignment of allreduce buffer. quantized kernels use 256-byte aligned temp buffers; if kv eviction moves the buffer, NCCL may fallback or behave unexpectedly. run this repro with REDWOOD_DEBUG_ALIGNMENT=1 to log pointers.

dmitri: Ran with both wait-event patch and DEBUG_ALIGNMENT=1. Results: no hangs in 30 runs. Alignment logs show buffers consistently 256-byte aligned in passing runs.

elaine: Great — suggests two things: 1) missing cross-stream sync between GC callbacks and collective entry, 2) fallback/fuzzy behavior when alignment changed + quant kernels. We should land the wait-event patch and add an assert/log for buffer alignment in the kernel selector.

ben: Agreed. Please capture a minimal unit test that reproduces the race (spawn small TP job with synthetic GC pressure) and add to eng-runtime CI. Also add regression test enabling REDWOOD_KERNEL_PREFERENCE to the test matrix.

dmitri: I'll prepare a PR: title "runtime: sync kv-evict with collectives to avoid NCCL timeouts". Will include the unit repro, alignment log, and opt-in telemetry metric 'kv_collective_race_hit'. Assigning to @alice for review.

alice: I'll review. Also propose we add a transient telemetry alert if kv_collective_race_hit > 0 per 1h on prod fleets so we can catch similar patterns in customer workloads.

carmen: Filed a follow-up to track: link: https://tickets/redwood/RT-4591

dmitri: Thanks all — circling back once PR is up. :pray:
